title: Inverse images along immersions preserve pro-etale limits
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $u:Y\to X$ be a locally closed immersion, meaning a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $u^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] preserves all small limits of sheaves of sets and of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every sheaf of commutative rings $R$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the inverse-image functor $\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(u^{-1}R)$, with module sheaves as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], is additive, exact, and preserves all small limits. Its underlying abelian sheaf is $u^{-1}$ of the underlying abelian sheaf, and its scalar action is $u^{-1}$ of the original action under the finite-product comparison. More generally, if $S$ is a ring sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $c:u^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ is a ring-sheaf isomorphism, then the functor $M\mapsto u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}R,c}S$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is exact and preserves all small limits, including countable products. Smallness is relative to the fixed sheaf universe. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed. The isomorphism hypothesis on $c$ is essential to this last assertion; no assertion is made for extension of scalars along a general ring map.

proof.text: For a weakly etale morphism, the over-category map is left adjoint to base change. Its sheaf restriction preserves all limits. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies this restriction with the specified pro-etale inverse image. Compare inverse image of a composite with the composite inverse images by composing adjunctions and using the base-change composition isomorphism. These arguments apply in particular to open immersions.

For an affine closed immersion the existing extra left adjoint makes inverse image a right adjoint, hence limit preserving by Mathlib. For a general closed immersion, inverse images of target affine opens are affine. Apply the Zariski-local preservation theorem to those affine closed restrictions. Factor a locally closed immersion using its closed lift to the coborder followed by the open inclusion, and apply preservation for the composite.

To compare abelian inverse image with set inverse image, identify abelian sheaves with commutative-group objects in set sheaves using the proved algebraic-structure equivalence. The direct-image restriction functor commutes with these group-object equivalences: its product and terminal comparisons are identities, and the given operation equations prove it respects zero and addition. Lift the set adjunction to commutative groups, transport across the equivalences and use uniqueness of left adjoints. The resulting natural underlying-set comparison transports all-limit preservation to abelian sheaves, because forgetting to sets preserves limits and reflects isomorphisms.

Use the module inverse-image comparison to obtain the natural abelian comparison and the generalized scalar-action graph assertion. The forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves preserves limits, as can be checked after the fully faithful sheaf-to-presheaf functor using sectionwise limits. It reflects isomorphisms, hence limits. Thus the abelian comparison transfers all-limit preservation to module inverse image. For finite colimits the same forgetful functor preserves and reflects them by the module-sheaf colimit API, and abelian inverse image preserves colimits by its adjunction. Additivity transfers through the natural comparison and the faithful additive forgetful functor.

Take the already constructed proEtaleRingModulePullback for the final functor; its objects and maps are definitionally the specified sheafified tensor extension after pure inverse image. Existing operations supply additivity and preservation of finite limits and colimits. For all limits, reuse the fully proved private tensor/restriction adjunction and scalar equivalence from the operations module by a proof-only import all. The adjunction uses the sheaf tensor-product universal property and sheafification. Restriction of scalars along a ring isomorphism is an equivalence, its inverse being restriction along the inverse ring map. Its inverse functor is another left adjoint to restriction. Uniqueness of left adjoints therefore identifies tensor extension with this equivalence inverse, so it preserves all limits. Compose with pure module inverse image.
